title: Normalize Aggregate null handling for missing categories
observed_behavior: Aggregating the uploaded `Profession` node field previously produced duplicate visible `null` rows and trimmed whitespace-sensitive labels such as `Other ` differently from the underlying uploaded value.
intended_behavior: Aggregate should normalize blank or missing categorical values into one stable display bucket and preserve or intentionally normalize visible category labels consistently so each displayed label is unique.
cause_summary: Aggregate used the raw uploaded field value as the bucket key and only substituted `null` at display time, so blank strings and missing values could survive as separate buckets even though they rendered the same. Trailing whitespace could also make the visible label drift from the stored value.
fix_summary: Normalized Aggregate group labels before counting by trimming string values and collapsing blank or missing values into one `null` bucket, then promoted the `Profession` regression into the maintained uploaded Aggregate spec.
notes: Closed after normalizing Aggregate bucket labels before counting. The uploaded `Profession` regression now runs green in the maintained Aggregate suite.

title: Refresh open Aggregate tables when filtering reclusters
observed_behavior: When Aggregate was already open and Minimum Cluster Size was raised from 1 to 3, the rendered `Node-cluster` table could stay stale even though the visible network had already dropped the hidden cluster. The visible percentages and rows still reflected the pre-filter state until the view was rebuilt.
intended_behavior: Aggregate tables that depend on visible cluster membership should recompute immediately when filtering changes cluster visibility while the Aggregate view stays open.
cause_summary: Aggregate only refreshed itself on a narrow `clusterUpdate$` path and did not have a reliable open-view refresh path for general network/filter updates.
fix_summary: Added a shared Aggregate table refresh path and wired it to `networkUpdated$`, `clusterUpdate$`, `onFilterDataChange()`, `onLoadNewData()`, and pane show so open tables stay synchronized after reclustering.
notes: Closed after the Minimum Cluster Size Aggregate refresh repro was re-enabled and verified green in the maintained uploaded controls spec.

title: Refresh Aggregate non-cluster tables after visibility changes
observed_behavior: When Aggregate was already open on a non-cluster table such as `Link-distance`, changing filtering so the visible links changed could leave the rendered aggregate rows stale. In the alternate-metric repro, the visible network correctly reduced to one link at distance `0.03`, but the Aggregate table still showed the old `0.01` and `0.02` rows.
intended_behavior: Aggregate tables based on visible node or link fields should recompute immediately when filtering changes the visible node or link set while the Aggregate view stays open.
cause_summary: Aggregate did not subscribe to a general open-view refresh signal for non-cluster node/link visibility changes, so filtering could leave open tables out of sync.
fix_summary: Reused the same shared Aggregate refresh path for all selected tables and triggered it from network/filter lifecycle hooks so non-cluster node/link tables update as soon as visibility changes.
notes: Closed after the non-cluster filtering Aggregate repro was re-enabled and verified green in the maintained uploaded controls spec.

title: Keep Aggregate tables isolated from timeline checkpoints
observed_behavior: With Aggregate open on the uploaded COVID timeline fixture, enabling Timeline and moving to the June 28 2021 checkpoint rebuilt `Node-*` and `Link-*` tables from the timeline-visible subset instead of the full filtered dataset, so row counts dropped from the pre-timeline baseline even though Aggregate is not a timeline-target view.
intended_behavior: Timeline checkpoints should change the global metrics and the Bubble Map and 2D datasets only. Aggregate node and link tables should keep using the non-timeline filtered dataset while the view stays open.
cause_summary: Aggregate computed node and link tables directly from `getVisibleNodes()` and `getVisibleLinks()`, which let the timeline visibility gate leak into a non-target data view.
fix_summary: Aggregate now uses the timeline-ignoring dataset getters for node and link tables, and the maintained isolation journey proves the rendered tables stay equal to the pre-timeline baseline while global metrics change.
